earlier_scan.source_named: Only source is Dalby 1963, The extinct language of Dama (short wordlist); no phonological description exists

sources.note: Nothing. States Dama is extinct, replaced by Mende, and that Dalby (1963) judged it Northern Mande (близ Kono/Vai) 'based on a few remembered words and toponyms'.

sources.citation: English Wiktionary contributors. 2020. Category 'Dama (Sierra Leone) lemmas' (c. 35 entries, e.g. 'bobama', 'makiɛ', 'buru', 'mɛnuwɛ', toponyms 'Kum-be-ku', 'Yumbokɔ', 'Nyali-kwɛ'), each entry referenced to Dalby, T. D. P. (1963), 'The extinct language of Dama', Sierra Leone Language Review 2: 50-54. en.wiktionary.org, entries last edited 6 August 2020; retrieved 2026-09-21.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Secondhand transcription of (apparently all of) Dalby's 1963 relic vocabulary and place-names: c. 20 lexical items (ba, ta, yi, ji, ma, manja, bole, buru 'house', sanja, dumai, fayi, bɛri, humbɔ, hɔmbɔ, kiaa, klaa, makiɛ 'good morning', mɛnuwɛ, sambai, yiba, bobama 'large swamp') and c. 13 toponyms (Widara, Mambia, Laai, Kum-be-ku, Kɔnjabui, Faai, Baji, Yumbokɔ, Nyaŋgɔ, Leve, Nyali-kwɛ, Yambe-kwɛ). Headwords use ɛ ɔ ŋ but carry no tone or stress marks and the entries contain no remark on pitch, tone or accent -- wordlist-only data, no statement. Its value: it shows the size and shape of the w…

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin F. 2006. K rekonstrukcii fonologicheskogo tipa i imennoj morfologii pra-mande [Toward a reconstruction of the phonological type and nominal morphology of Proto-Mande]. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana / Trudy Instituta lingvisticheskih issledovanij 2(2). St Petersburg: Nauka.
sources.note: Nothing about Dama prosody; Dama is mentioned once, as a pointer. The monograph-length article reconstructs Proto-Mande phonological type (including tone) from living languages; Dama contributes no data.

sources.citation: Brenzinger, Matthias (ed.). 1992. Language Death: Factual and Theoretical Explorations with Special Reference to East Africa. (Contributions to the Sociology of Language 64.) Berlin; New York: Mouton de Gruyter. ISBN 3-11-013404-7. [copies we hold = the whole 456-page volume; target-language coverage is in Sommer, Gabriele, 'A survey on language death in Africa', pp. 301-417 (doi:10.1515/9783110870602.301), with minor mentions in Batibo, 'The fate of ethnic languages in Tanzania', pp. 85-98, and Legère, 'Language shift in Tanzania', pp. 99-115]
